Answered 'ok' on 2026-10-03 04:06Z, 2026-10-05 and 2026-10-07; connect timeout on 2026-10-14. | Both builds launch a headless Chrome at the /e/ path and request /p/ in VirusTotal sandbox output. :8146 is absent from all 15 Hunt.io port-history rows and all 14 protocol rows, so its presence, closure or continued service is NOT CHECKED; the 2026-10-14 rescan probed the root path rather than the historical /e/ path. | The response body is the two bytes 'ok' as application/xml from Python BaseHTTP. Two limits travel with it: the address held unrelated services before the 2026-04-01 announcement of the prefix (do not match pre-April history on it), and the bpupdate.exe and exp.html surface here is tied to the address by IP only, authorship NOT CHECKED. | The service sits on a host that is HIGH-confidence operator infrastructure, but the two builds that request it are tied to it by IP only and their authorship is NOT CHECKED (a developer or vendor pipeline is not excluded). Prefer the two paths as the indicator; the cloudedge-edge/1.4 banner has no measured base rate. [confidence 80/100]

ipv4: 38.180.16.98. Hard-coded literal IP in Relay.java.new with no DNS lookup and a 15 s connect timeout. The relay opens the connection and writes READY2 first (7 bytes), sends PING every 15 s while idle, accepts one controller line of the form DIAL <host> <port>, replies OK or FAIL, then splices the two sockets byte for byte with no encryption or framing. Confirmed on the wire in a contained lab run on 2026-10-09 (22 of 22 sessions opened with READY2 alone) and in the operator's own listener log (1,051 relay check-ins: 648 labelled READY(pod) and 403 READY2(wls)). Relay times are undated. The listener was never observed by any scanner, which is a coverage gap, not evidence that it did not exist. Confidence: the endpoint role is HIGH, a historical role covering both relay lanes (pod and wls); DEFINITE applies only to the READY2 protocol bytes of the wls-variant file in the contained 2026-10-09 run, and which file was deployed is not established. | Reported as an open directory to Hunt.io (two automated warnings, 2026-09-27 and 2026-09-30); VirusTotal shows 0 malicious engines. The last positive directory listing is 2026-10-08 19:45Z (9,917 files). Silence onset is undated and the 2026-10-09 zero-response window came from one egress only: whether the host is down or that egress is blocked is NOT CHECKED. The directory was serving 1,649 root files by 2026-10-01 against the 362 captured on 2026-09-30, so the served tree is far larger than the capture. | Part of the same Zabbix join as the :9090 callback; the byte-level script-to-listing relationship was not independently proved and the reader left the listener's role unidentified. | The listener log reads 'listening on 0.0.0.0 port 9090'; the decoded operator script creates a global script z-revtest that connects here and sends id;hostname. The join of script to log is rated MODERATE by the lane (no run log, timestamp or Zabbix audit row) and the callback has no timestamp; the owner of the calling host is unattributed (victim-estate association only). | A legitimate DNS server on TCP/53 speaks DNS framing; this service speaks plain ASCII and answers nothing until the relay announces itself. Match the TCP/53 flow whose first payload is the line READY2 (hex 52 45 41 44 59 32 0a). A TCP/53 flow with no DNS message parsed is the generic hunt. | Do not block this address outside the operator window or on the ports not listed here. The address carried a mail/web tenant in 2024 and a Windows tenant from 2024-12 to 2025-07; its :443 certificate, its JARM and every SSH host key row belong to those earlier tenants. The operator surface is :53, :80, :111, :445, :4000, :8899, :9090 and :9443 from 2026-09-26. | A held 26-byte startup line only; no arrival of any path map is shown. Do not treat a hit on this port as proof of collection. | Port 9090 is common. The discriminating artifact is the callback itself: a Zabbix global script on a proxy or agent connecting outward to this address and returning root identity and hostname. Alert on the outbound conjunction from a monitored host, not on the port alone. [confidence 80/100]

ipv4: 38.180.196.193. Operator use HIGH, operator control MODERATE: the operator's own batch84.sh calls it 'our IP (vpsbr)' and a payload is staged there. A later grade superseded a 2026-10-03 LOW on control. JARM, SSH host key and certificate fingerprints for this host were excluded from this feed rather than carried at an upgraded confidence. | Referenced by wls_rce.sh and wls_rce2.sh as the payload server; a session on 2026-09-30 stages pwn.xml there. 'cadsus' appears in 0 of the 973 files of the :8899 archive, so the realm label does not describe the panel's content. | Block this host-and-port pair rather than the address: the address is co-tenanted. The discriminating response is HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="cadsus-panel". | Co-tenanted host. Ten third-party parked domains (gaspowered, gastromono, gastronomiaboliviana, gastronomiaperuana, gateandfences, gatelights, gavickmagazine, garagedoorrepairtulsa, gayathens, gaybrussels) still resolved to this address through 2026-10-03, and that parked-DNS traffic is not this operator's. Prefer blocking the service ports in the operator window (2026-08-20 to 2026-09-14) over the address alone. A blanket block of the address would take unrelated tenants with it. [confidence 60/100]

Attribute.value:
title: GLPI htmLawed Test Page POST Request (CVE-2022-35914, Renamed Copy Included)
id: 20c855ee-9086-444b-885c-59a6abba56c1
status: experimental
description: >-
    Detects a POST request to a PHP file inside GLPI's bundled htmlawed vendor directory.
    The unauthenticated command execution in CVE-2022-35914 is reached through the htmLawedTest page, and an operator tool read in this case posts to a copy that had been renamed with a suffix, so the match uses the directory and not the default file name.
    A GLPI web root should never serve its vendor directory.
references:
    - https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/opendirectory-38-180-16-98-brazil-public-sector-toolkit-20261015-detections/
    - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-35914
author: The Hunters Ledger
date: 2026-10-09
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1190
    - cve.2022-35914
    - detection.emerging-threats
    - stp.3
logsource:
    category: webserver
    definition: 'Requires web server access logs that record the request method and URI, for example Apache or nginx access logs on the GLPI host or the reverse proxy in front of it, with the full request URI mapped to cs-uri-query as the other SigmaHQ webserver rules do. The request body is not in these logs, so the match is on method and path only.'
detection:
    selection:
        cs-method: 'POST'
        cs-uri-query|contains|all:
            - '/vendor/htmlawed/htmlawed/'
            - '.php'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Unlikely
level: high
Attribute.comment: GLPI htmLawed Test Page POST Request (CVE-2022-35914, Renamed Copy Included) | TIER: Detection | robustness 2 | confidence HIGH | ATT&CK T1190 | rule hash 18cfb033 | https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/opendirectory-38-180-16-98-brazil-public-sector-toolkit-20261015-detections/

Attribute.value:
title: Java Process Spawns Shell to Rewrite Log Files
id: 410da2b6-3023-4f5f-a9a2-1e7abf0c3783
status: experimental
description: >-
    Detects a shell spawned by a Java process whose command line combines grep -v with a .log file pattern.
    Read from an operator's request body that rewrites every log file under a WebLogic domain home without the lines naming a planted JSP, through a temporary file and a copy back.
    Hunting rule, because legitimate Java launched maintenance scripts also filter logs.
references:
    - https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/opendirectory-38-180-16-98-brazil-public-sector-toolkit-20261015-detections/
author: The Hunters Ledger
date: 2026-10-09
tags:
    - attack.stealth
    - attack.t1070
    - stp.3
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: linux
    definition: 'Requires Linux process creation telemetry that records the parent image and the full command line of the child, for example auditd EXECVE records joined to the parent process, Sysmon for Linux EID 1, or an EDR sensor with equivalent fields.'
detection:
    selection:
        ParentImage|endswith: '/java'
        Image|endswith:
            - '/sh'
            - '/bash'
            - '/dash'
        CommandLine|contains|all:
            - 'grep -v'
            - '.log'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Log housekeeping scripts started from a Java based scheduler or management agent
level: medium
Attribute.comment: Java Process Spawns Shell to Rewrite Log Files | TIER: Hunting | robustness 2 | confidence LOW | ATT&CK T1070 | rule hash be5feb93 | https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/opendirectory-38-180-16-98-brazil-public-sector-toolkit-20261015-detections/

Attribute.value:
title: Shell Process Creates a JSP File Under a WebLogic _WL_internal Directory
id: f3c8d853-4507-4818-9883-a79f977a41a9
status: experimental
description: >-
    Detects a shell creating a .jsp file below a _WL_internal directory.
    WebLogic's own Java process extracts web application contents there, so a shell as the writing process marks a file placed from outside the deployment path.
    Read from an operator's request body that writes a command-execution JSP into every subdirectory of every _WL_internal and stage directory under a domain home.
references:
    - https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/opendirectory-38-180-16-98-brazil-public-sector-toolkit-20261015-detections/
author: The Hunters Ledger
date: 2026-10-09
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.t1505.003
    - stp.3
logsource:
    category: file_event
    product: linux
    definition: 'Requires Linux file creation telemetry that records the creating process image and the target path, for example Sysmon for Linux EID 11 or an EDR sensor with file creation events. auditd path rules on the WebLogic domain home would also work but are not default.'
detection:
    selection:
        TargetFilename|contains: '/_WL_internal/'
        TargetFilename|endswith: '.jsp'
        Image|endswith:
            - '/sh'
            - '/bash'
            - '/dash'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Administrators extracting or copying JSP files into WebLogic temporary directories by hand during troubleshooting
level: high
Attribute.comment: Shell Process Creates a JSP File Under a WebLogic _WL_internal Directory | TIER: Detection | robustness 2 | confidence MODERATE | ATT&CK T1505.003 | rule hash 36e0f998 | https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/opendirectory-38-180-16-98-brazil-public-sector-toolkit-20261015-detections/

Attribute.value:
title: WebLogic Java Process Spawns Shell Writing a JSP Into a WebLogic Internal Directory
id: 67f6efc3-d491-446b-99c9-26dec7274776
status: experimental
description: >-
    Detects a shell spawned by a Java process whose command line names a WebLogic _WL_internal directory and a .jsp file.
    This is the process-level footprint of a remote command-execution request (the XMLDecoder-in-WorkContext shape sent to the WS-AT endpoint)
    that plants a command-execution JSP into WebLogic staging directories.
    The behaviour was read from an operator's request body that finds every _WL_internal and stage directory under the domain home and writes one JSP into each subdirectory.
references:
    - https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/opendirectory-38-180-16-98-brazil-public-sector-toolkit-20261015-detections/
author: The Hunters Ledger
date: 2026-10-09
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.t1505.003
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.004
    - stp.3
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: linux
    definition: 'Requires Linux process creation telemetry that records the parent image and the full command line of the child, for example auditd EXECVE records joined to the parent process, Sysmon for Linux EID 1, or an EDR sensor with equivalent fields.'
detection:
    selection:
        ParentImage|endswith: '/java'
        Image|endswith:
            - '/sh'
            - '/bash'
            - '/dash'
        CommandLine|contains|all:
            - '_WL_internal'
            - '.jsp'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - WebLogic deployment or patching scripts started from a Java based tool that copy JSP files into exploded application directories
level: high

Attribute.value:
title: Zabbix Daemon Child Process Touching Credential Files or Instance Metadata
id: 7fc3ea3a-98a7-4a97-877a-a8a4dbfefc48
status: experimental
description: >-
    Detects a child process of a Zabbix server, proxy or agent daemon whose command line names the password digest file, shell history, authorized keys, the cloud instance metadata address or nmap.
    Read from an operator's Zabbix API scripts that create global scripts and system.run items to run exactly these requests on a proxy and on monitored hosts; no output of them was held.
    Hunting rule, because monitoring administrators legitimately run commands through the same daemons.
references:
    - https://the-hunters-ledger.com/hunting-detections/opendirectory-38-180-16-98-brazil-public-sector-toolkit-20261015-detections/
author: The Hunters Ledger
date: 2026-10-09
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1072
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.credential-access
    - attack.t1552
    - stp.3
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: linux
    definition: 'Requires Linux process creation telemetry that records the parent image and the full command line of the child, for example auditd EXECVE records joined to the parent process, Sysmon for Linux EID 1, or an EDR sensor with equivalent fields.'
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '/zabbix_server'
            - '/zabbix_proxy'
            - '/zabbix_agentd'
            - '/zabbix_agent2'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/etc/shadow'
            - '.bash_history'
            - 'authorized_keys'
            - '169.254.169.254'
            - 'nmap '
    condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
    - Monitoring items or global scripts that deliberately check authorized_keys or shell history for compliance
